Assistant A's claim that the request is "not possible" is misleading: an O(log(min(n, m))) algorithm also satisfies an O(n) upper bound, and a linear-time O(1)-space two-pointer merge would work as well. Even so, A gives a correct, well-known binary search solution with O(1) space, which satisfies the constraints, since O(log n) is within O(n). Its code is correct.

Assistant B's code has flaws. It slices lists, which copies and uses O(n) extra space, and the recursion uses stack space. There is also a bug: when `i = min(k//2, len(nums1))` and `j = k - i`, `j` can exceed `len(nums2)`, and the standard algorithm uses j = k//2 for both arrays. With i = k//2, j = k - i is about k/2 as well, so this can partially work, but the recursion discards `i` elements from nums1 when `nums1[i-1] <= nums2[j-1]`. This is only valid if i + j = k, with i elements discarded being safely among the k smallest. Using j in the comparison with i + j = k is not correct in general, because discarding is only safe when the pivot is within the first k-1 elements. Taking nums2[j-1] with j = k - i makes the comparison valid only in some cases, and the code can be wrong. The claim of O(1) space is also false, given the slicing and recursion. The explanation is also inaccurate.

A is correct and better.

[[A]]
